correctness.rationale: Every nonadjacent pair in K_3 tensor K_n, n>=3, has distance two. Splitting same-column and same-row pairs gives exactly |A_i|>=2 and |A_j union A_k|>=3, with no omitted cases. The four disjoint enumerator cases partition by numbers of size-two row complements; maximality follows from safe shrinking of any larger row complement, including size three. Independent common-neighbor brute tests of all 299520 subsets for n=3..6 verify coefficient and maximality formulas. The random limit follows from three independent binomial-to-Poisson limits and an O(n^-2) union bound for duplicate two-subsets; the asymptotic is proved, not inferred from tests.

value.rationale: The first-factor-three case is a structurally exceptional unaddressed boundary of the established direct-product theory: six omissions per optimum are needed instead of the four-omission construction available in the large-width setting. The exact polynomial describes all feasible monitoring configurations, the pure facet characterization gives all locally maximal configurations and their multiplicity, and the Poisson window measures robustness under random node selection. These are natural quantities for the specified product, not arbitrary parameter slices.
